hasel.t: Hasel, M. G. (1994). 'Israel in the Merneptah Stela'. Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research 296: 45–62.

faust.t: Faust, A. (2006). Israel's Ethnogenesis: Settlement, Interaction, Expansion and Resistance. London: Equinox.

garr.t: Garr, W. R. (1987). 'A Population Estimate of Ancient Ugarit'. BASOR 266: 31–43.

gilibert.t: Gilibert, A. (2021). 'Urban Squares in Late Bronze Age Ugarit: a Street View on Ancient Near Eastern Governance'. Journal of Near Eastern Studies 80(2).

schachner.t: Schachner, A. (2017). 'Hattusa and its Environs: Archaeology'. In M. Weeden & L. Z. Ullmann (eds), Hittite Landscape and Geography. Leiden: Brill, 37–49.

schachner2024.t: Schachner, A. (2024). 'A new look at an ancient city: An outline of the chronological and urban development of the Hittite capital Ḫattuša'. Anatolian Studies 74: 13–46.

zuckerman.t: Zuckerman, S. (2007). 'Anatomy of a Destruction: Crisis Architecture, Termination Rituals and the Fall of Canaanite Hazor'. Journal of Mediterranean Archaeology 20(1): 3–32.

abbas.t: Raafat Abbas, M. (2017). 'The Town of Yenoam in the Ramesside War Scenes and Texts of Karnak'. Cahiers de Karnak 16: 329–341.

soleb.t: Soleb temple of Amenhotep III (Sudan), toponym list: 'land of the Shasu, yhw'. Reading as the divine name Yahweh is disputed; summary with references.

aram.t: Oxford Bibliographies: 'Aram' (earliest undisputed mention of Arameans in inscriptions of Tiglath-pileser I, c. 1112 BC).

kaniewski.t: Kaniewski, D. et al. (2011). 'The Sea Peoples, from Cuneiform Tablets to Carbon Dating'. PLoS ONE 6(6): e20232. (Destruction of Gibala-Tell Tweini, kingdom of Ugarit, dated c. 1192–1190 BC)

millek.t: Millek, J. M. (2018). 'Destruction and the Fall of Egyptian Hegemony over the Southern Levant'. Journal of Ancient Egyptian Interconnections 19: 1–21. (Egypt's withdrawal was gradual, over 75 years or more; Jaffa perhaps c. 1125 BC)

fink1995.t: Finkelstein, I. (1995). 'The Date of the Settlement of the Philistines in Canaan'. Tel Aviv 22: 213–239. (Argues for c. 1135 BC instead of the usual c. 1175 BC)

feldman.t: Feldman, M. et al. (2019). 'Ancient DNA sheds light on the genetic origins of early Iron Age Philistines'. Science Advances 5(7): eaax0061.

smith2002.t: Smith, M. S. (2002). The Early History of God: Yahweh and the Other Deities in Ancient Israel. 2nd ed. Grand Rapids: Eerdmans. (El and Baal in Canaanite religion; the name Israel containing El)

yon2006.t: Yon, M. (2006). The City of Ugarit at Tell Ras Shamra. Winona Lake: Eisenbrauns. (Ugaritic alphabetic cuneiform of thirty signs; the city not reoccupied after its destruction)

yurco1990.t: Yurco, F. J. (1990). '3,200-Year-Old Picture of Israelites Found in Egypt'. Biblical Archaeology Review 16(5): 20–38. (Karnak 'Ashkelon wall' reliefs attributed to Merneptah; one scene read as Israel)

stager1985.t: Stager, L. E. (1985). 'The Archaeology of the Family in Ancient Israel'. Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research 260: 1–35. (Pillared house, ground floor for animals and storage, upper storey for living)

kingstager.t: King, P. J. & Stager, L. E. (2001). Life in Biblical Israel. Library of Ancient Israel. Louisville: Westminster John Knox. ISBN 0-664-22148-3. (Diet, bread as staple, grinding stones, farming)

meyers2013.t: Meyers, C. (2013). Rediscovering Eve: Ancient Israelite Women in Context. New York: Oxford University Press. (Grain processing as daily, largely women's work; estimates of hours per day)

kochavi1977.t: Kochavi, M. (1977). 'An Ostracon of the Period of the Judges from 'Izbet Ṣarṭah'. Tel Aviv 4: 1–13. (The Izbet Sartah abecedary; its date and script are debated)

mazar1982.t: Mazar, A. (1982). 'The “Bull Site”: An Iron Age I Open Cult Place'. Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research 247: 27–42. (Hilltop shrine in northern Samaria with a bronze bull figurine)

garfinkel2012.t: Garfinkel, Y., Streit, K., Ganor, S. & Hasel, M. G. (2012). 'State Formation in Judah: Biblical Tradition, Modern Historical Theories, and Radiometric Dates at Khirbet Qeiyafa'. Radiocarbon 54(3–4): 359–369. (2.3 ha, casemate wall, two gates, short-lived, destroyed c. 1000 BC)

garfinkel2015.t: Garfinkel, Y. et al. (2015). 'King David's City at Khirbet Qeiyafa: Results of the Second Radiocarbon Dating Project'. Radiocarbon 57(5). (17 burnt olive pits from the destruction layer, dated to about 1000 BC)

garfinkelganor2009.t: Garfinkel, Y. & Ganor, S. (eds) (2009). Khirbet Qeiyafa Vol. 1: Excavation Report 2007–2008. Jerusalem: Israel Exploration Society. (Incl. R. Kehati, 'The Faunal Assemblage', 201–208: no pig bones)

maeir2008.t: Maeir, A. M., Wimmer, S. J., Zukerman, A. & Demsky, A. (2008). fink2011ful.t: Finkelstein, I. (2011). 'Tell el-Ful Revisited: The Assyrian and Hellenistic Periods (with a New Identification)'. Palestine Exploration Quarterly 143(2): 106–118. (Rejects Tell el-Ful = Gibeah of Saul)

lichtheim1976.t: Lichtheim, M. (1976). Ancient Egyptian Literature, Vol. II: The New Kingdom. Berkeley: University of California Press. mazar1980.t: Mazar, A. (1980). Excavations at Tell Qasile, Part One: The Philistine Sanctuary: Architecture and Cult Objects. Qedem 12. Jerusalem: Hebrew University. (Temple of strata XII, XI and X, each rebuilt larger)

grayson1991.t: Grayson, A. K. (1991). Assyrian Rulers of the Early First Millennium BC I (1114–859 BC). RIMA 2. Toronto: University of Toronto Press. (Tiglath-pileser I, A.0.87: campaigns against the Arameans, march to the Mediterranean)

kitchen2003.t: Kitchen, K. A. (2003). On the Reliability of the Old Testament. Grand Rapids: Eerdmans. (Maximalist position; David c. 1010–970 BC, chronology pp. 82–83)

josephusapion.t: Josephus, Against Apion 1.106–127 (quoting Dius and Menander of Ephesus on Hiram of Tyre and the Tyrian king list); also Antiquities 8.144–149.

bible.t: Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), cited by book and verse in each line. Religious tradition, written down centuries after the events it tells.

ephal1982.t: Eph'al, I. (1982). The Ancient Arabs: Nomads on the Borders of the Fertile Crescent, 9th–5th Centuries BC. Jerusalem: Magnes Press / Leiden: Brill. (Gindibu 'the Arab' at Qarqar, 853 BC, the earliest mention of Arabs)

dearman1989.t: Dearman, J. A. (ed.) (1989). Studies in the Mesha Inscription and Moab. Archaeology and Biblical Studies 2. Atlanta: Scholars Press. fink2000.t: Finkelstein, I. (2000). 'Omride Architecture'. Zeitschrift des Deutschen Palästina-Vereins 116(2): 114–138. (Samaria, Jezreel, Megiddo and other royal centres: platforms, casemate walls, moats)

otto2003.t: Otto, S. (2003). 'The Composition of the Elijah–Elisha Stories and the Deuteronomistic History'. Journal for the Study of the Old Testament 27(4). meshel2012.t: Meshel, Z. (2012). Kuntillet ʿAjrud (Ḥorvat Teman): An Iron Age II Religious Site on the Judah–Sinai Border. Ed. L. Freud. Jerusalem: Israel Exploration Society. (Inscriptions 'Yahweh of Samaria and his Asherah' and 'Yahweh of Teman and his Asherah'; c. 800 BC)

bendorfink2023.t: Ben-Dor Evian, S. & Finkelstein, I. (2023). 'The Sheshonq Fragment from Megiddo: A New Interpretation'. Bulletin of the American Schools of Oriental Research 390: 97–111.
